paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: worry can't do what we hope it will do. Jesus asks, "Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?" (Luke 12:25). Worry feels like work, but it never gets the batch out of the oven, and all it ever added for me was dust.

So what do we do with the fear? Jesus says the Father already knows what you need (Luke 12:30). He feeds the ravens, He clothes the lilies, and Jesus says, "how much more valuable you are than the birds!" (Luke 12:24). If you're that valuable to Him, you can put the 2 a.m. list down.

Then Jesus points us somewhere better to look: "But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you." (Luke 12:31). He tells His little flock not to be afraid, because their Father is pleased to give them the kingdom (Luke 12:32), and then tells them to sell their possessions and give to the poor, with a treasure in heaven where no thief approaches and no moth destroys (Luke 12:33). That's the part that makes me look at my oven mitts, because Jesus says, "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also." (Luke 12:34). So, friend, what are you holding tight, and where is your heart sitting today?
